subject: TNF inhibitors: tuberculosis signal; Tyenne biosimilar recall
headline: TNF inhibitors: tuberculosis signal; Tyenne biosimilar recall

highlights.sentence: Tuberculosis was reported more often than expected with TNF inhibitors (PRR 7.54).
Tyenne, a tocilizumab biosimilar, is under a Class I recall for presence of particulate matter.
FDA added warnings for heart events, cancer, clots and death to JAK inhibitors.
A safety trial found a higher risk of heart problems and cancer with Xeljanz.
Imuldosa, an ustekinumab biosimilar, is under a Class II recall for lack of assurance of sterility.

preheader: Also: FDA warnings on JAK inhibitors and an Imuldosa recall.
signal_caveat: A reporting signal is not proof a drug caused an event.
disclaimer: For research and informational purposes only. Not medical advice. Do not stop or change any medication without talking to your doctor. FAERS is a spontaneous-report system with under-reporting, duplicate reports, and no exposure denominator. A disproportionality signal means a reaction was reported more often than expected. It is not an incidence rate. Report adverse events to FDA MedWatch.
fda_caveat: There is no certainty that the reported event was actually due to the product. The information in these reports has not been scientifically or otherwise verified as to a cause and effect relationship and cannot be used to estimate the incidence of these events.

items.title: TNF inhibitors · Tuberculosis
items.body: Tuberculosis was reported more often than expected with TNF inhibitors than with all other FAERS reports (PRR 7.54, 95% CI 7.28–7.82). This is a disproportionality signal. The reporting odds ratio is 7.56 (95% CI 7.29–7.84). This meets the Evans screen: at least 3 reports, a PRR of at least 2, and a chi-square of at least 4. The ratio is not an incidence rate.
